venue.name: City of Totems Totem Tour Walk
venue.description: Duncan calls itself the City of Totems and has more than 40 totem poles standing outdoors around its downtown core, carved by Indigenous artists from Cowichan Tribes and many other First Nations. A self-guided walking route is marked by yellow footprints painted on the pavement, and each pole carries a sign with the carver's own story. A Digital Totem Tour adds video, written material and audio recordings through QR decals beside the poles. The City of Duncan owns and runs the collection, and its pages describe no admission charge, no booking and no guided or school version.
restrictions: If you plan to use the totem images for commercial or promotional use, please fill out a Totem Image Use Application and submit to duncan@duncan.ca for consideration and approval

programs.name: Self-guided totem pole walk
programs.description: A walking route through downtown Duncan past more than 40 totem poles, marked by yellow footprints painted on the pavement. Every pole has an interpretive sign giving the carver's name and the story the pole tells, gathered in oral history interviews with the carvers and their families. Beside the poles are QR-coded decals that open videos, written material and audio recordings, and the same Digital Totem Tour can be opened online before you go. The City publishes no printed route map, no brochure and no set start or finish point.
programs.what_children_do: Walk the downtown sidewalks following yellow footprints painted on the pavement, stopping at each pole to look up at it. At every stop there is a sign with the carver's story, and a QR decal an adult can scan so the group can watch a short video or listen to a recording about that pole.
programs.our_note: You set the pace and can turn back whenever the group has had enough, which suits mixed ages. There is no map or brochure published, so load the digital tour on a phone before you leave or plan to follow the painted footprints. Nobody meets you and nothing is booked, so sort out washrooms and lunch yourself before you set off.
programs.practical_summary: This is an outdoor walk on public streets and sidewalks, with no washrooms, no indoor lunch space and no wet weather fallback named anywhere. Bus parking and how long the route takes are not stated either, so a call to the City is worth it before a big group comes.
programs.evidence: Embark on a journey of culture and history by following the yellow footprints and start the self-guided walking tour

gaps: No guided version and no school or daycare programme is mentioned anywhere on the City site. A site search for a guided or school totem tour returned only council agendas, so whether a led tour can be arranged is unknown.
No route map, brochure or PDF is published. The interactive Digital Totem Tour is hosted off the City's own site at onthisspot.ca, so it was not used as a source.

No starting point or meeting place for the walk is published. The address recorded here is Duncan City Hall at 200 Craig Street, which is the only street address the site gives and sits in the downtown core where the poles are, so the pin should be treated as approximate.
How long the walk takes, how far it is, and whether the route is step free are all unstated.
Washrooms, indoor lunch space, wet weather fallback, bus parking and stroller access are unstated. It is a public street walk, so a director should plan these independently.
No age guidance, no capacity limit and no contact for group questions. The only number published is the general City Hall line, 250.746.6126.
No price is stated anywhere. It is recorded as free because it is a walk on public streets with no admission point, ticket or booking route published.
The parent Totems Tour page was last updated in January 2024 and the Totem Tour Walk page in August 2026, so the digital tour description is the more current of the two.
The page has no og:image, so the hero was taken from the lead photo on the Totems Tour page.
months unknown: the site does not say whether the digital tour or the signage is available year round, though the poles are outdoors and permanent.
